It makes the next CI E2E failure readable to anyone, and the Linux container reproduced a real intermittent E2E failure. But I couldn't read the assertion from CI's own failed runs, so whether that failure is what kept CI red is likely but unproven.

- **Branch / commit:** `main` @ `841ca69823a2e71e6a97e5c1d01c12babdccd2ea`, authored by Otohime <quiinthieu@gmail.com>. Getting it onto `main` took three rebases after two non-fast-forward rejections; nothing was force-pushed.
- **CI:** run 40310239199 was still pending when I stopped. I didn't watch it; the green gate and QA judge that.

**Failure messages are now public.** GitHub job logs need a token (HTTP 403), but check-run annotations don't. Under GitHub Actions, `scripts/e2e.mjs` now adds a reporter (`scripts/e2e-annotate.mjs`) that turns each failed test into an error annotation with its file, line and assertion, plus a section in the run's summary page. When E2E fails, the CI step also adds the server's last 80 lines and the build, Node and Chrome versions to that summary. The step still exits with the suite's own status, and production still waits for checks. A regression test covers the reporter, with a run outside Actions as the negative control.

**Reproduced defect: the Kame "hold to pet" test.**
- **What failed:** before the fix, `e2e/kame.test.ts:90` failed in 2 of 3 full E2E runs in an Ubuntu container.
- **Why:** Playwright's fake clock keeps moving with real time until it is paused. On a busy host, the real milliseconds around the 499 ms step pushed it past the 500 ms threshold. The test's assumption was wrong; the Kame component is fine.
- **The fix:** the clock now pauses before the check. With that change the container passed 3 of 3 runs, all 91/91.
- **Duplicate repair:** commit 9ddd084 (pm-259/t-1583) landed the same fix on `main` while I was working. I dropped my copy, and my commit adds only a negative control: with the clock running, 50 real ms plus the same 499 ms step already pets Kame.
- **Link to CI:** Kame first appeared in dd21add, and CI has gone 3 red and 2 green on the same code since 15fd171. That fits, but only a red run's annotation will confirm it.

**Still open:**
- **Ryugu "Page already revealed" error** (owner pm-256/t-1559): not reproduced on macOS Chrome 156 or in 6 container runs. I found a possible cause: React ignores only the exact message "Transition was aborted because of invalid state", so a longer Chromium message would surface as a page error. I didn't change any source on that basis because it's unconfirmed.
- **New: a React hydration mismatch (#418) on `/projects`**, seen once in 8 runs of the Kame test file on macOS. It didn't recur in 20 targeted runs, 60 page loads or the container runs, so it's reported, not fixed.
- **Footer failure in run 40277523350:** its log is unreadable (403), so the cause stays unknown. The footer walk and Chromium matrix pass now.
- **`author.txt` contents:** task-manager returns only its hash and size, and no likely author line matches the hash. The git author on 15fd171 is Otohime with no co-author line.

**Checks:**

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm test` | 2123/2123 |
| `npm run lint` | exit 0, no errors |
| `npm run typecheck` | exit 0 |
| `npm run build` | exit 0 |
| Footer walk | 67 ok, 0 failed |
| Footer Chromium matrix | 171 ok, 0 failed |
| `npm run test:e2e` | 102/102 |

That full run was against b0befb6 plus my commit. After the last rebase, which only changed `lib/plan-release.test.ts` and `scripts/probe-plan-release.mjs`, I reran unit tests (2127/2127), lint and typecheck, but not the build, footer or E2E checks.

The report is `projects/pick-up-this-plan-https-apps-vietky-io-vn-plans-plans-pm-242/t-1564-summary-run-8822.md`, and `commits.txt` is in the shared artifacts folder. I recorded the decisions and a lesson on the plan, and submitted the summary report. The report names 9ddd084 as t-1573; the correct id is t-1583.

While restarting a test server early on, I ran a broad `pkill -f "next start"`. The sandbox wouldn't let me list processes, so I can't confirm it hit only my own server. After that I stopped processes by PID only.
